;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[War in Afghanistan (2001–2021)]]
**[[Afghan Armed Forces|Afghan forces]] launch ground and air operations against the [[Taliban]], killing 51 of them in nine [[provinces of Afghanistan|provinces]] of the country. Afghanistan's [[Ministry of Defense (Afghanistan)|Ministry of Defense]] say that the military conducted thirteen ground offensives and twelve airstrikes. In the northern province of [[Balkh Province|Balkh]], local officials say that three women and four children were killed. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-afghanistan-attacks-surge/afghan-forces-launch-air-ground-attacks-on-taliban-killing-51-idUSKBN1ZP0EG (Reuters)]
*[[Syrian Civil War]], [[Northwestern Syria offensive (December 2019–March 2020)]]
**[[Syrian Armed Forces|Syrian government forces]] retake several cities in the [[Idlib Province]] area, amid a push from [[Syrian President]] [[Bashar al-Assad]] to recapture the last rebel strongholds. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-syria-security/syrian-government-forces-capture-towns-in-advance-on-rebel-held-idlib-idUSKBN1ZP0FC (Reuters)]
*[[Mali War]]
**Nineteen [[Malian Armed Forces|Malian soldiers]] are killed in an attack on an [[army camp]]. No group has claimed responsibility. [https://www.france24.com/en/20200126-mali-militant-attack-army-camp-al-qaeda-islamic-state-sokolo-niono-kill (France24)]
*[[2019–2021 Iraqi protests]]
**Amid further heavy clashes in [[Baghdad]] rockets hit the United States embassy injuring at least one. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/01/iraq-rockets-hit-baghdad-green-zone-anti-gov-protests-200126195616176.html (Al Jazeera)] [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2020/jan/27/us-embassy-iraq-rocket-attack-injuries (''The Guardian'')]

;Arts and culture
*[[62nd Annual Grammy Awards]]
**[[Billie Eilish]] sweeps the major categories winning [[Grammy Award for Song of the Year|Song of the Year]], [[Grammy Award for Record of the Year|Record of the Year]], [[Grammy Award for Album of the Year|Album of the Year]], and [[Grammy Award for Best New Artist|Best New Artist]]. [https://www.latimes.com/entertainment-arts/music/story/2020-01-26/billie-eilish-sweeps-major-categories-2020-grammys (''Los Angeles Times'')]

;Disasters and accidents
*[[2020 Brazilian floods and mudslides]]
**At least 39 people are dead in the [[Brazil]]ian [[States of Brazil|states]] of [[Minas Gerais]] and [[Espírito Santo]] after heavy rains hit the country's [[Southeast Region, Brazil|southeast region]]. [https://veja.abril.com.br/brasil/minas-registra-cinco-mortes-por-causa-das-chuvas-e-buscas-continuam/ (VEJA)]
*[[2020 Calabasas helicopter crash]]
**Retired [[NBA]] player [[Kobe Bryant]], his daughter [[Gianna Bryant]], [[College baseball|baseball]] [[Coach (baseball)|coach]] [[John Altobelli]], and six other people are killed in a helicopter crash in [[Calabasas, California]], U.S. [https://abcnews.go.com/US/dead-helicopter-crash-southern-california/story?id=68545466 (ABC News)]

;Health and environment
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Mainland China]]
***A leading group on the prevention and control of the outbreak is established, led by Chinese Premier [[Li Keqiang]]. The leading group decides to extend the [[Chinese New Year|Spring Festival]] holiday to contain the outbreak. [http://www.xinhuanet.com/english/2020-01/26/c_138735589.htm (Xinhua News)]

;Politics and elections
*[[2020 Peruvian parliamentary election]]
**People in [[Peru]] head to the polls to elect the members of the country's [[Congress of the Republic of Peru|congress]] after its dissolution in September 2019. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-latin-america-51208274 (BBC News)]
*[[2019 Trump–Ukraine scandal]]
**An unpublished manuscript of former [[National Security Advisor (United States)|National Security Advisor]] [[John Bolton]]'s book ''[[The Room Where It Happened]]'' reveals that [[President of the United States|President]] [[Donald Trump]] told him that unfreezing military aid to [[Ukraine]] was conditional on their performing investigations into [[Joe Biden]] and [[Hillary Clinton]]. [https://www.nytimes.com/2020/01/26/us/politics/trump-bolton-book-ukraine.html (''The New York Times'')]
